title: Information Flow Loops
hook: Collecting data you never look at is just a fancy way of guessing.
statement: Systems only get better when feedback actually changes what you do next.
explainer: Plenty of founders track numbers and then run the same play anyway. The loop only works when a review leads to a real change you can point to.
sop: List the routines you run regularly: marketing, ops, health, money.
Pick one output for each that you can actually measure.
Set a fixed weekly or monthly review time.
Change one input based on what the last review showed.
Write down what you changed and why, so the next review has a comparison.
equation_example: Current score is 60, and your Feedback adjustment adds 15. 60 + 15 = 75. A rising Next State means the loop is working. Flat or falling means you're collecting feedback, not using it.
question: Name one thing you run every week with zero feedback on whether it's working.
closing_statement: No feedback means you just repeat the same mistakes.
caption:
Principle Nº 191: Information Flow Loops

Collecting data you never look at is just a fancy way of guessing.

Systems only get better when feedback actually changes what you do next.

Your turn: Name one thing you run every week with zero feedback on whether it's working.
